title: High-Probability Characteristic in 10-Round KNOT-256
summary: The 10-round KNOT-256 differential was not exhaustively analyzed at or below average probability 2 to the minus 66, leaving open whether an omitted characteristic is unexpectedly likely under the default constants.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the 10-round KNOT-256 differential has an omitted characteristic $C$ with $p_{\mathrm{avg}}(C)\le 2^{-66}$ but unexpectedly high probability under the default constants.

scope.domain: Fixed-key differential cryptanalysis of the 10-round KNOT-256 differential under its default round constants.
parameters: 10 rounds: the analyzed KNOT-256 round count
2 to the minus 66: the upper bound on the characteristic's average probability
Default round constants: the fixed constants under which unexpectedly high probability is sought
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether an omitted characteristic at or below the average-probability bound has unexpectedly high probability under the default constants.

citations.label: Differential Cryptanalysis in the Fixed-Key Model

progress.summary: The source reports zero probability for the examined characteristics through selected average probabilities down to 2 to the minus 65, while those at 2 to the minus 66 or lower were not exhaustively analyzed. It argues that a high-probability characteristic is unlikely because each can be nonzero for only a very small fraction of round constants.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Differential Cryptanalysis in the Fixed-Key Model
